text:
harper: quick sync from RFC follow-up: we need a concrete delegation playbook for when a project-scoped key needs to act across projects. goals: minimize blast radius, preserve DX for infra/CI, and keep audit clear. ideas?

nina: propose 3 patterns: 1) service-lease via exchange, 2) scoped "proxy" roles (capability sets), 3) temporary org keys for emergency with strong audit.

luis: how are capability sets defined? per-route is too noisy. i'd group by intent: read_only, generate, manage_deploys, billing_read. policies apply to sets.

wanda: +1 for intent groups. keeps policy counts manageable. also add "sensitive_admin" for dangerous ops which require 2-person approval.

harper: sample UX flows:
- CI runner: uses project key -> registers service -> requests lease to target project -> exchange returns service-bound token TTL 30m.
- Human admin: hits console to request temporary cross-project org-key -> approval workflow -> key issued TTL 24h.

nina: exchange API sketch:
```
POST /auth/v1/exchange
{ "source_key": "proj-AAA", "target_project": "infra", "capability_set": "manage_deploys", "actor": "svc/ci-123" }
# response: { "token": "slt-...", "expires_in": 1800, "aud": ["infra"] }
```

luis: important: token should carry origin metadata (orig_key_id, actor_id, policy_id) so telemetry correlates request to owner. log at both exchange and target gateway.

wanda: ops: enforce mTLS + KMS-wrapped signing for issued tokens. mark tokens non-exportable. throttle exchanges per-origin.

security-bot: policy: require policy match for capability_set; flagged 0 inconsistencies.

harper: migration path thought: default new keys = project-scoped. existing org keys get "legacy" flag and we surface usage. run analytics for 60d then auto-suggest replacements using exchange for top flows.

nina: fallback: we should allow a "cross=true" attribute for keys created via API for 90 days to reduce breakage, but warn and show risk and set expiry.

luis: question: who can register a service? restrict to repo owners or CI admins and require a one-time owner approval. registration should create a service-id and policy whitelist.

wanda: add console affordance: "Register service for cross-project access" -> pick target projects and capability sets -> owner approves -> service gets registration id. generate an onboarding token for pipelines.

harper: SDK changes: credential provider that uses the project key to call exchange and refreshes seamlessly. avoid client-side browser exposure. emphasize server-only flows.

nina: telemetry dashboard needs: active legacy org keys, top callers of exchange, failed exchange attempts by policy, average TTL, and highest-frequency target projects. SOC needs alert on sudden spike in exchanges.

luis: emergency escape hatch: short-lived admin org-token minted via ticketed workflow that requires 2 approvals and logs in immutable audit. use only as last resort.

wanda: ops note: map rate-limits to original key owner, and add circuit-breaker for noisy origins. also add quota cost accounting so billable customers see exchange costs.

security-bot: detected one internal endpoint without client cert requirement -> filed infra-issue #1292.

harper: open question for RFC: should capability sets be extendable by org admins? i think yes but default canonical sets should exist. document extension process.

nina: agree. add a governance page: how to propose new capability set, risk review checklist.

luis: also include migration CLI/tool that scans code repos for org-key usage patterns and suggests minimal capability sets for replacement.

wanda: next steps: harper will draft delegation playbook + sequence diagrams, nina will draft telemetry/dashboard reqs, luis will draft capability set taxonomy and sample policies. I'll schedule ops readiness review.

ops-bot: scheduled canary: auth-exchange v0.9 -> us-east-1 at 2025-07-01T04:00Z.

harper: thanks all. I'll open the follow-up PR with those artifacts. ping if you want edits before I land it. :pray:
